To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
tandem pore domain halogenated K+ channel (THIK) 1 and THIK 2 form active heteromers in the plasma membrane.
THIK1-THK2 heterodimers are active channels with intermediate biophysical properties.
the THIK1 and the THIK2 subunits assemble and form active heteromultimeric channels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the assembly of THIK subunits and the generation of heterodimers.
the molecular and functional properties of tandem pore domain halogenated-inhibited K+ (THIK) channel subunits.
the assembly and function of tandem pore domain K+ channels.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have demonstrated that THIK1/2 form heteromeric channels.
THIK1/2 heteromers are active and that THIK1 is able to mask the ER retention motif of THIK-2.
the THIK1/2 subunits are able to heteromerize, forming active channels with intermediate properties, but that this is not their physiological function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the THIK1-THIX2 heterodimer is an active channel with properties that differ from THIK1 and from THIK2 homodimers, and this channel may be relevant in vivo.
THIK1-THK2 heteromers are active channels that can contribute to cell excitabilty.
THIK1/2 form heterodimeric leak K+ channels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the THIK1/2 subunits assemble and form functional heteromers.
THIK1/2 form heteromeric channels that contribute to the background K+ current in cells and tissues co-exposing THIK1 and 2.
THIK1 is able to form functional homodimers and heterodimers with THIK2.
